newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-ANALYSIS OF SAMPRAS V CLAVET.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-ANALYSIS OF SAMPRAS V CLAVET.

text.p: Analysis of Wednesday's French Open men's singles second round match between top seed Pete Sampras of the U.S. and Spain's Francisco Clavet, won 6-1 6-2 6-2 by Sampras.

A superb winning backhand allowed Sampras to break Clavet in the second game and lead 2-0. The world number one broke his opponent again in the fourth game with the Spaniard hitting a forehand too long on break point. Sampras remained on top and waited for Clavet to hit a return into the net on set point.
Both players held serve in the first four games, but in the fifth Sampras earned five break points and finally converted when Clavet missed an easy backhand to build a 3-2 lead.

Sampras went on to break the helpless Spaniard again and lead 5-2. Clavet then managed to save a set point with a little help from the net cord but Sampras earned another one on which Clavet hit a backhand long.
Clavet saved two break points in the opening game, but in the third he lost his serve through an unforced error to allow Sampras to go 2-1 up.

A blistering return gave Sampras another break for a 4-1 lead. Both players held serve in the next two games and Sampras served for the match, opening up a 40-0 lead. He sealed it with a forehand winner on his first match point.
